chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “Wash your garment from the urine of that whose flesh is not eaten.”
And this indicates that what is eaten for its flesh does not require washing, as we have explained in more than one place.

key_terms.أَبْوَالِ: Urines; referring to the urine of animals.
key_terms.اِغْسِلْ: Wash; an imperative command indicating legal obligation in context.
key_terms.ثَوْبَكَ: Your garment or clothing that is subject to purification.
key_terms.غَسْلُهُ: Its washing; the act of cleansing the impurity from the garment.
key_terms.مَا لَا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: That whose flesh is not eaten; animals not lawful or not normally eaten.

ai.seo_question: Does urine from animals whose meat is not eaten make clothing require washing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding ritual purity of garments, specifically requiring washing from the urine of animals whose flesh is not lawful to eat. It also indicates, by implication, that the urine of animals whose flesh is eaten does not require washing in this context.
